title: The Cane with Nicola Walker - review
transcript: the cane at the Royal Court Theatre London written by mark Ravenhill directed by Vicki Featherstone and starring Nicola Walker Maggie steed and Alan Armstrong a much-loved teacher is about to retire but his home is under siege his estranged daughter has come to visit her parents it's his regular use of the cane years ago that appears to have sparked the protests and it seems that the protests may be more against the old ways of doing things the patriarchal society in which men dominated through the use of violence I'm not sure how much I believe the set up or indeed the ending but mark Ravenhill has written a tremendous script that not only creates a tense atmosphere and powerful dialogue as the characters prowl around each other and take vicious swipes it also provides a lot of thought because although the play is primarily about the teacher it's also about any of us who work for or deal with institutions the daughter is heavily involved in academies and it seems she has a rigid belief in her institution as much as her father believes in his we gain insights into why the father inheriting a culture of violence continued it because it was his duty which sounds very like I was only obeying orders but his daughters no angel she's manipulative and coercive and in trying to get her own way she doesn't want reconciliation she wants revenge and we see her too flaring into violent language and acts of violence nothing distracts from what the characters say and do and all three actors give subtle nuanced performances Maggie steed is the oppressed bullied proudly loyal but also nasty when cornered wife Alun Armstrong with calm reasonableness red-faced anger and underlying weakness all somehow present at the same time whichever one is being displayed and Nicola Walker Wow so natural in the way she talks and moves so incredibly still when she's observing the others making her reasonable characters unreasonable behavior deeply disturbing I give the cane four stars if you this review please subscribe to one minute theater reviews you
